title: Supported cube flip relay
summary: The left arm holds a large shallow tray with a cube on it, and the right arm holds a small flat pusher. The left arm must first bring the tray to a presentation point. The right arm must then tip the cube over onto an adjacent face. It does so with a short push that sets the cube rotating and ends before the cube is half-way over, so that the cube completes the tip on its own momentum and settles on the tray. The left arm then moves the cube, on the tray, to a new place, and the pusher tips it a second time in the same way, so that the cube's original bottom face ends up on top. Finally the tray must carry the correctly oriented cube to an output point and hold it there. The cube must never leave the tray.
robot_setup: Two Pandas facing each other along x. panda-0 (left): base at (-0.55, -0.22, 0), yaw 0 (facing +x). Its tool is a tray with a 5 mm floor, inside 0.24 x 0.24 m (2 x `left_tool_half`, 0.12 at this instance), with walls 12 mm high and 5 mm thick on all four sides. The tool frame is the centre of the inside floor surface, z up, x pointing away from the arm's base. With the tray level the hand points straight down and the floor centre is 0.12 m ahead of the gripper TCP along tool x and 0.04 m below it. The grey adapter enters at the middle of the back (tool -x) wall: a 12 mm wide post protrudes 6 mm inward from the floor up to 35 mm, and a bar protrudes 12 mm inward 29-41 mm above the floor, above the 12 mm wall. Start: floor centre at (0.04, -0.035, 0.23), level, axes aligned with the world. panda-1 (right): base at (0.74, 0.22, 0), yaw pi (facing -x). Its tool is a pusher: a small rigid plate 8 mm thick (along tool x), 50 mm wide (tool y) and 12 mm tall (tool z), with the tool frame at its centre and x normal to its face, pointing away from the arm's base. The pusher centre is 0.12 m ahead of the TCP along tool x and 0.04 m below it. A grey adapter (a horizontal bar from the hand and a short post) ends about 5 cm behind it on the hand side; plate and adapter form one rigid tool link. Start: pusher centre at (0.16, 0.02, 0.268), rotated 180 deg about z (face normal = world -x, toward the tray). Role labels per phase (left, right): support_presentation: tray_support, preparing_pusher; first_inertial_flip: moving_support, impulse_pusher; second_contact_geometry: repositioning_support, cleared_pusher; second_inertial_flip: moving_support, impulse_pusher; oriented_output: oriented_carrier, cleared_pusher.
scene: A plain orange cube (44 mm edge, all faces alike) starts resting flat on the left tray's floor, near the tray centre and a little toward the pusher's side (+x). Its axes start aligned with the world axes. There is nothing else in the scene, and nothing moves by itself. The table top is the world's z = 0 plane.
scene_privileged: Cube: half extent `cube_half` = 0.022 m, mass `object_mass` = 0.05 kg, friction 0.65, restitution 0.25. At reset it is placed at rest, unrotated (its local axes equal the world axes), at (0.06, y0, 0.23 + `cube_half` + 0.0005), with y0 ~ U(-0.038, -0.032) (the only random draw; nothing is drawn later). That is 20 mm toward +x from the tray centre and 0.5 mm above the floor. Tray: mass `left_tool_mass` = 0.22 kg, friction `left_tool_friction` = 0.65. Pusher: mass `tool_mass` = 0.2 kg, friction `tool_friction` = 0.3. Tool restitution 0.05. The `friction` parameter (0.65) is listed in the config, but the cube's friction is hard-coded to the same 0.65. Table friction `table_friction` = 0.08. `radius`, `incoming_speed`, `fixture_speed`, `preview` and `restitution` are not used by this task. Horizon `horizon` = 25 s.

phases.name: support_presentation
phases.text: the cube is on the tray (it has touched the tray's tool link within the last 25 ms) while the tray's tool frame is within 0.025 m of the presentation point (0.08, 0.015, 0.23).

phases.name: first_inertial_flip
phases.text: an inertial flip, judged only from pusher contacts made in this phase. The tilt of a cube axis means the angle between that cube-local axis and world vertical; here the tilted axis is the cube's local z (initially up). (a) The pusher (any part of its tool link) touches the cube; the tilt at the last moment of contact is the release angle. (b) Early release: at some moment more than 0.02 s after the last pusher contact, the cube is untouched by the pusher, the release angle was between 0.03 rad and pi/4 - 0.02 = 0.765 rad (about 1.7 to 43.9 deg), and the cube turns faster than 0.4 rad/s. This is recorded once. (c) Inertial crossing: after the early release, the tilt grows from at most 45 deg (pi/4) at one physics step to more than 45 deg at the next. (d) After that, the final state must hold for 0.25 s without interruption: the cube's local +x axis (the face that initially faced +x, toward the right arm) points up within 0.18 rad (about 10.3 deg), the cube moves slower than 0.05 m/s and turns slower than 0.3 rad/s, and it is on the tray (touched within the last 25 ms). The cube's world position at the moment this phase completes is recorded.

phases.name: second_contact_geometry
phases.text: with the cube on the tray (touched within the last 25 ms) and not touched by the pusher at that moment, the cube's centre is more than 0.025 m (world distance) away from the position recorded at the end of first_inertial_flip.

phases.name: second_inertial_flip
phases.text: the same inertial-flip rule as first_inertial_flip, judged only from pusher contacts made in this phase, with the cube's local x axis (now pointing up) as the tilted axis. That is: a pusher contact, then a release with tilt between 0.03 rad and 0.765 rad followed (more than 0.02 s later, still untouched) by an angular speed above 0.4 rad/s, then the tilt of local x passing 45 deg. The final state is that the cube's local -z axis (its original bottom face) points up within 0.18 rad, with speed < 0.05 m/s, angular speed < 0.3 rad/s and the cube on the tray, for 0.25 s without interruption.

phases.name: oriented_output
phases.text: for 0.5 s without interruption: the cube is on the tray (touched within the last 25 ms) and its local -z axis points up within 0.18 rad; the tray's tool frame is within 0.025 m of the output point (-0.04, 0.16, 0.25); and the cube moves at less than 0.04 m/s relative to the tray. This completes the task.

task_failures: cube_lost_from_tray: at any time, the cube's centre in the tray's tool frame is 0.115 m or more from the floor centre along x or y (|x| or |y| >= 0.115 m), or 0.01 m or more below the floor surface (z <= -0.01 m).

flip_recontact_before_balance: during first_inertial_flip or second_inertial_flip, the pusher touches the cube after an early release has been recorded in that phase but before the 45 deg inertial crossing. An early release that does not lead to a crossing therefore leaves no retry: any further pusher contact in that phase fails the task.
contact_rules: The tray and the pusher (each its whole tool link, adapter included) may touch the cube only, not the table. No other part of either robot, the fingers included, may touch anything. The two arms and their tools may never touch each other, and no arm may touch itself.
world_goals_fixed: Presentation point (0.08, 0.015, 0.23) for the tray's tool frame (support_presentation), announced at reset as `goal_target`; output point (-0.04, 0.16, 0.25) for the tray's tool frame (oriented_output), announced as `goal_goal`.
difficulty_note: Each flip must be a short impulse that ends while the cube is still well below 45 deg yet leaves it enough rotation to tip over by itself, with no second touch allowed once a qualifying release has happened. The cube then has to settle on the correct face on a tray that the other arm holds, and between and after the flips the tray must carry it without letting it slide out.
standard_notes: Nothing moves at t = 0 (the cube just settles onto the tray). All faces of the cube look the same, so its orientation (which face is up) can only be followed by tracking its rotation from frame to frame.
